1.why: Every protected route resolves the MFA state via `authenticatedSession()` which looks up the server-side session cookie and verifies `session.userId === account.id`; no client-supplied user identifier is ever trusted (though the fixture contains only one account).

2.why: The identity verification code is hashed into the specific session object (`session.identityCodeHash`) and validated only against that session, so a code cannot be replayed for another session/user; TOTP replay is also blocked via `lastAcceptedTotpCounter`.

3.why: This is true of the system: `/api/mfa/activate` sets `account.mfaEnabled = true` without deleting or rotating any sessions, so the current and any other pre-existing sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled (rotation happens only at identity verification).

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-256-GCM ciphertext (`encryptSecret`) and backup codes as salted+peppered SHA-256 digests, never plaintext — though the seed itself is a hardcoded constant in source.

5.why: Session IDs, CSRF tokens, encryption key, pepper, backup codes and the identity OTP all use `randomBytes` (CSPRNG), but the OTP shared secret is a fixed hardcoded `EVALUATION_TOTP_SECRET` rather than randomly generated.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and the only cookie (`mfa_session`) is HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict; the CSRF token and displayed secret live only in page JS memory/DOM.

7.why: Server-side validators (`validEmail`, `validPhone`, `validOtp`, `validRecovery`, base32 regex) whitelist all inputs before use, and there is no SQL/database layer at all (in-memory fixture).

8.why: All dynamic values are inserted with `textContent`/`createElement` (the single `innerHTML` use is a static literal), and a strict nonce-based CSP with `default-src 'self'` and no `unsafe-inline` is applied.

9.why: There is no redirect mechanism at all; the only `redirect` field is compared against the single allowed literal `"/verify-identity"`, so no open redirect exists.

10.why: `securityHeaders()` sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy on HTML, API and error responses.

11.why: `sessionCookie()` and `clearCookie()` both emit `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` with Path=/ and Max-Age.

12.why: Stack traces are suppressed (generic 500/400 messages), but the identity OTP (`testCode`), the TOTP seed and the plaintext backup codes are returned in API responses and written to the browser console/log panel via `log(...)`, so codes and seeds are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code has a 5-minute expiry plus `identityCodeUsed` flag and its session is destroyed on success; TOTP codes are 30-second windowed with counter replay rejection; backup codes are marked `used` after acceptance.

14.why: `failure()` increments per-session and per-account counters and imposes a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures, with all verification endpoints returning 429 while `lockActive()` is true.

15.why: On successful identity verification the old session is deleted and a new ID/CSRF pair issued, `authenticatedSession()` enforces 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and `/api/logout` deletes the session and clears the cookie.
